timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Howdy, I'm Jeffrey Snowver. I'm a technical fellow at Microsoft and these days I'm very
much focused in on Azure and management. So I'm spending most of my days on Azure Stack,
but we also have Azure Portal, Azure Hardware, and of course, as all the Azure management
stuff, including PowerShell. Well, let's see, I've been involved with PowerShell since
2001 when I invented it. I wrote the Core Monad Manifesto then and then have been bringing
it to bear. Of course, that date then it was Monad. Now it's PowerShell, so whatever we
made that change. I guess that was 2006, we decided to call it PowerShell. Yeah, so right
now I'm using PowerShell quite extensively. Of course, we build PowerShell, but we also
use PowerShell extensively to manage Azure. In particular, I'm focused a lot of these days
on Azure Stack. Azure Stack is where we allow Azure, the public cloud, to be able to run on
customers' data centers, starting as low as four servers. So think about that. How do I run
like a public cloud on four servers? And the answer is, it's a lot of hard work. I guess
what we're doing to do that hard work. And the answer is PowerShell. PowerShell and
desired state configuration. Indeed, we have, I think someone coming the other day, we've
got like over 250,000 lines of PowerShell to configure, deploy, update, and maintain,
and secure Azure Stack. So I'm not just a producer of PowerShell, I am a consumer of PowerShell.
Yeah, I think it's incredibly important that everyone be competent with PowerShell. I mean,
I don't really think you can call yourself a Windows IT Pro. If you're not competent
with PowerShell, then there's being an expert in PowerShell. And here's the deal. The
people who are experts at PowerShell, I talked to a lot of them, and they all have had
significant advances in their careers because they are PowerShell experts. They've got new
jobs, they've got new responsibilities, they've got promotions, and they've got a lot more
pay. So it's definitely been one of the things that we sought out to do and we've achieved,
which is for the people who have learned this technology, their careers have advanced
and benefited greatly. Yeah, so whenever I come to these conferences, I always learn something
new, I always enjoy listening to the security things. The security guys, think and use your
tools in ways you never would have thought of, and then we got to go produce, you know,
find the flaws, find the vulnerabilities, and go patch them. So I learned a lot of new
things about how the security guys use our tools to both attack and defend customers.
The thing I love the most about this conference is talking to the people. They're incredible
people, they're doing fantastic stuff with PowerShell, and it's a great environment. The talks
talks are great, but after each one of the talks, we're having these great coffee sessions,
coffee break sessions, where you're able to meet the people, talk extensively. Really, it is,
you can sit at home and you can watch the videos, but you can't have the coffee breaks and talk
to the people. That's what makes this conference so special.
